serious_competing_readings.whole_rival_argument: **“The irritation is only a disguise for affection.”** The inquiry after withdrawal, returned letter and anticipated ice cream make a hidden-attachment interpretation plausible. It remains an interpretation rather than a mutually accepted label. Kazusa states aversion, asks for noninterference, refuses sentimental names and ends angry at another challenge. The stronger synthesis preserves care and refusal as compatible rather than requiring the latter to be false. No romance claim or global “tsundere” rule is needed to explain these local choices. [K:L111,L124,L138; A:L201; L17:L28]

**“Reisa pursues only justice.”** Her public heroic purpose, voluntary protection, responsibility and actual restraint give that reading serious evidence. Her explicit happiness at rediscovery, sadness over exclusion and ordinary need for friends complicate a solely mission-based explanation. Connection and justice can motivate the same approach, while neither guarantees adequacy to Kazusa. Conversely, the personal element cannot justify replacing every useful patrol or kite rescue with a story of obsession. [K:L111,L139; R:L416–429,L447]

**“Kazusa needs to suppress the old self completely.”** Her erasure language and embarrassment support this as an earlier self-appraisal. Her later café account says exact imitation and total forgetting went too far. She can refuse legend publicity without denying that a history belongs to her; the important distinction is who decides when and how that history enters company. The remembered girl's identity and a complete psychological cause remain unresolved. [L07:L28–34; L16:L28–38]

**“The adult produces a benevolent reconciliation.”** Sensei gives time, inquiry, command help and an audience; Kazusa explicitly values consulting. But the photograph lapse, apologies, teasing alternatives, partial understanding and Reisa's privacy condition prevent an omniscient-plan account. Three represented explanations of watching over Kazusa are alternatives, not one secretly completed masterplan. Peer and student actions remain independently causal. [L06:L30; L07:L26,L34; L16:L24–26,L38; K:L126]

**“A later welcome repairs all earlier consent.”** The purchased ice cream, expanded invitation and acceptance are strong achieved positives. They establish that Reisa can be welcomed in a particular setting. They do not retrospectively retract the request for noninterference, identify the unnamed accuser in another object or narrate future duel consent. The public contexts are independently compared without a fabricated global later date. [A:L188,L201,L237; L09:L28; L17:L28]

**“A boundary account drains the comedy of its point.”** The source does contain delighted rhetoric, appetite jokes, grand names, embarrassment and the frustration of a renewed challenge. Those pleasures belong to their actors; an analysis that discards them would be incomplete. It is equally incomplete to treat comic presentation as proof that every recipient enjoyed the act or every blast was harmless. The coexistence of play, actual care, gratitude, consent limits and renewed irritation is part of the narrative construction. [K:L113,L146–148; L17:L24–36]

**“The failed ending cancels the withdrawal and rescue.”** Reisa's resumed challenge is decisive contrary evidence to permanent cessation. It does not make heard boundaries, protective withdrawal, Kazusa's concern or returned company unreal. The stronger causal claim is local capacity for revision under available evidence, vulnerable to distorted transmission, rather than either complete cure or complete inability to change. This is retrospective literary explanation, not a validated prediction about the next encounter. [K:L111,L138–142; L17:L26–36]

**“The private variants prove a simple developmental ladder.”** Written magical-girl pleasure, practical interventions, ordinary music and chosen memory broaden the repertoire. They do not date every costume against the event, make conditional UI lines enacted incidents or turn repeated special passages into independent corroboration. The comparison concerns differences of wanted activity and recipient response, while actual sequence is confined to supported local anchors. [R:L431–457; P:L427–444; K:L60–72]

**“Reisa is isolated; Kazusa is the necessary cure.”** The challenge and loss can be read as a concentrated bid for contact. Reisa explicitly reports kind classmates and invitations, others' offers of adjustment and successful fun after trying advice. Kazusa's private independent life is also broader than this relation. Their importance to one another is more exact when neither is made the other's total social world or treatment. [R:L416–425; P:L413–444; K:L111]

**“Quiet food and leisure are merely decorative after the real crisis.”** Kazusa locates an earlier motive for life change in the café's warmth; Reisa treats friends' play as indispensable; private authored company is received positively; the band hospitality contains actual initiative and welcome. Those are explanatory and achieved ends. Keeping them does not erase failed publicity, fatigue or danger; it lets the argument specify what the participants hope protection and correction make possible. [L16:L28–38; R:L420–425; A:L201]
